turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, sorry, this computer is crawling. Give me a moment... okay. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, it's this cough. It will not go away, and I'm really scared something is wrong.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): A cough. How long are we talking?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It started after the flu. That was six weeks ago. The flu itself went, but the cough stayed, the whole six weeks.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's at it all night. I sleep down the passage and it still wakes me.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, it's worse at night. I lie down, this dry tickle starts, and then I can't sleep. Is that a bad sign? Should I have come sooner?
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say the night bit again. I clicked the wrong window.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Night-time, when I lie down. In the day I cope, it's just annoying. At night it's hectic.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any phlegm with it, or any blood?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly dry. In the morning there's a little bit of clear stuff, not green. No blood. I check every time, I'm frightened of seeing blood.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): And fever, right now?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not now. I was hot and shivery with the flu, but that finished. Nothing like that anymore.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Or short of breath?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No pain. And I'm not short of breath, not even on the stairs at work. It's only the cough. Why the heart questions? Is it my heart?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Just covering the list. Have you lost weight?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I haven't lost weight. My appetite is fine, I'm eating the same.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thembi, your work trousers are hanging. You showed me the belt this morning.

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually... ja. The clothes are loose. I took the belt in. I just didn't think of it as weight loss when you asked. Yoh. Is this cancer? People say cough plus weight is cancer.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hold on, don't rush me into a name. This screen has frozen again. One moment.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Please don't go quiet on me. Is it cancer or not? I need you to say.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been like this all week, same questions, and Google at two in the morning. We even argued in the bakkie coming up the hill.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): I missed half of that, the fan on this machine is loud. The clothes, say it once more?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I said no, and then it clicked. The trousers are loose, two holes on the belt. So something has come off. I can't tell you how many kilos.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any travel lately? Out of the province, or overseas?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No travel. Work and home, that's my life. I haven't been near an airport in years.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone around you sick with TB? Fair question with a cough this long.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't know a single person with TB.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about cousin Naledi in Pietermaritzburg? Auntie said they started her on TB treatment. You drove through and took her food.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): That was not TB. Auntie always makes it bigger. It was an ordinary chest infection, and I stood at the gate, I never went inside. So, no contact. I'm sure of that.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm only repeating Auntie. She was quite definite about the TB tablets. I don't want to fight, but that's what she said.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can't decide that from here. We'll park it. Medicines... the file says amlodipine, ten milligrams, every morning, for your blood pressure.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten? No, doctor. It's five milligrams. The sister at the clinic cut it down. Five, every morning.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The box I fetched from the chemist says amlodipine ten. I can still picture the label.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): That box is the old one. Please don't write ten. I take five milligrams, one tablet in the morning, and I don't skip days.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): So my screen says ten and you say five. I'm not guessing. I'll leave the dose off until we see the bottle. You are still taking it, though?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, every day, for the blood pressure. It's been years. Could the cough be from the amlodipine? I read that some tablets make you cough.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Some pressure tablets do that. Amlodipine usually doesn't. I'm not pinning this cough on the tablet, and I'm not pinning it on anything else yet.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Then what are you thinking? The flu that never left, TB, a tumour? Just tell me which one, even if you're not sure.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): What I won't do is pick one today. Post-viral cough, reflux, a lingering infection, TB, a mass, that whole list floats past. I am not writing any of them down as what I think this is. There isn't enough in front of me.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She also wants to know about work. She does the admin at the primary school, and she's worried about the children.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the school, say that again? I was reading an old note.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I do admin at the primary school, and I've been going in. Must I stop? If this is TB I shouldn't be near the kids, né?
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not quarantining you on a guess. Come, let me listen. Deep breath in... and out. Once more.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breath sounds are clear. I don't hear crackles, and I don't hear a wheeze.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Clear is good, isn't it? Then why is the cough still here after six weeks? Clear doesn't mean it's nothing. Does it?
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clear only means I can't hear a pneumonia sitting here. I want a chest X-ray, and I'll book it at radiology.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): An X-ray. Is the radiation a lot? Will the medical aid pay, or is it cash? And how long before you actually see the result?

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's an ordinary chest film, not a big dose. Medical aid usually covers it when the indication is this cough. The report often comes back in a day or two, longer if radiology is stacked.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): If it's bad, will you phone, or must I just wait and stew? I can't do two weeks of not knowing.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks and we'll go through the film together. If you start coughing blood, or you get short of breath, don't wait for me, go to casualty.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Okay. What must I bring? And which amlodipine dose are you going to put on the file?
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bring the bottle from home so we can see whether it's five or ten. I'm not changing the tablet today. Keep taking whatever you've actually been taking.
[SEG0053] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll look tonight. There might be two boxes in the cupboard, eish. We'll bring both.

[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Last thing, sorry. For the night cough, can I prop myself on an extra pillow? And is a mixture from the chemist safe, or will it clash with my tablet? I don't want to make this worse.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): An extra pillow is fine if sleeping a bit upright helps. Leave the chemist cough mixture for now, until we know what we're dealing with. Reception will point you to radiology on your way out.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Doctor says can't hear pneumonia; not a full exam finding of absent pneumonia signs.
Conflict exists, but speaker is family member, not explicitly sister.
bad.text: The patient denies any tuberculosis contact, while her sister says a cousin was started on TB treatment. (type=conflicting_statement, related_entities=negative_findings[6]; medical_history.family_history[0], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: Cough is described as mostly dry, with daytime symptoms milder/annoying and night-time symptoms much worse when lying down.
No current weight measurement is known: patient reports loose trousers and needing two tighter belt holes but cannot say how many kilograms lost.
No shortness of breath even on stairs at work.
Doctor advised not to quarantine or stop work based only on a guess about possible TB.

Doctor discussed differential possibilities without committing to a diagnosis: post-viral cough, reflux, lingering infection, TB, and a mass/tumour were all considered possibilities but none diagnosed.
Doctor stated the chest exam being clear means he cannot hear a pneumonia at present, rather than proving nothing is wrong.
Chest X-ray was to be booked at radiology, and reception would direct the patient to radiology on the way out.

Doctor counselled that a standard chest X-ray is 'not a big dose' of radiation, medical aid usually covers it for this indication, and the report often returns in 1–2 days though longer if radiology is busy.
